trace.title: Metric contract
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

Prometheus commonly scrapes exposed metrics and stores time series. Grafana can query/display data from selected sources.

A dashboard is a view over a data contract, not an independent guarantee that the service is healthy.

Counters accumulate events; rates describe change over time. Gauges describe a current value.

Histograms can help examine latency distributions under their configuration. Choose labels with bounded categories.

A ticket ID per metric label can create an enormous number of series.

Setup: define one task-relevant metric, expose it safely in a training service, configure a scrape, create a query/panel, and trigger a synthetic failure. Then write an alert with an owner and runbook.

Consider hosted alternatives or Datadog when their operating model fits better; using both stacks is not mandatory.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
App records bounded metric → collector observes → query transforms over a time window → panel/alert presents it → investigator checks user outcome.

A missing scrape and a true zero value are different things.

For a latency claim, ask which requests were included and whether errors/timeouts were excluded. A low median can coexist with painful tail latency.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail:
A mean alone can hide a slow minority. Unbounded labels can overwhelm the system.

A pretty dashboard with no action/owner can fail silently during an incident.
